title: gpu-cost-benchmark-playbook
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures our most recent synthetic benchmark runs across the candidate inference instance types (NVIDIA A10, L4, A100, H100) and translates them into engineering and product-friendly metrics for the Optimize cost model (tokens/sec, $/hour, $/token, perf/W). The goal is to have a repeatable playbook and a canonical set of numbers to feed into the optimizer recommendations engine and Dedicated capacity pricing.

Quick summary (first-pass):
- H100: best raw throughput and perf/W on FP16/AMP for long sequences; highest $/hour but best $/token for large batches and high concurrency.
- A100: strong middle ground. Better perf/W than A10 but worse than H100 across most loads. Good candidate for reserved capacity where latency SLOs moderate.
- L4: cost-efficient for small models and low-concurrency text generation; excellent $/token for embeddings and small-context chat.
- A10: cheapest on hourly price but limited perf/W; competitive for small seq/low-batch use with INT8 quantized models.

Benchmark context and assumptions (important):
- Workloads: 3 synthetic scenarios run for each model/instance combo: short-chat (seq_in=64, seq_out=64), long-completion (seq_in=512, seq_out=512), and embedding-only (batching up to 512 vectors). We also run a tail-latency pass (P99) with interleaved small requests to capture latency SLOs.
- Models: gpt-medium-ish family (7B float/8-bit quant), gpt-13B-ish (FP16), and a 70B variant FP16/quant. For private deployments customers will pin specific model versions; this sheet assumes model shapes that are representative but not exhaustive.
- Batching policy: continuous batching with max_batch_size set per instance class to reflect realistic runtime limits (A10: 32, L4: 64 for small models, A100: 128, H100: 256).
- Power: perf/W is measured as tokens/sec per watt (averaged across a 5 minute steady-state window). Power draw measured via DCGM where available; otherwise manufacturer TDP used as upper bound with note.
- Pricing basis: list hourly prices used are internal reserved/spot blended rates matching our cloud cost numbers (confidential). $/token derived from measured tokens/sec and $/hour.
- Tooling: runs executed with inference-bench v0.9 (see linked GH PR). Commands are in the linked GH PR; key flags: --seq_in N --seq_out M --batch_size B --quant q8|q4 --streaming false.

Raw table (representative rows) — columns: instance, model_size, fp_mode, batch, tokens_per_sec, power_watts, perf_per_watt, $_per_hour, $_per_token, p99_latency_ms, notes
A10 | 7B | q8 | 16 | 18,200 | 180 | 101.1 | 0.95 | 0.9 | low-memory headroom, good for INT8 workflows
A10 | 13B | fp16 | 8 | 9,100 | 200 | 45.5 | 0.95 | 1.6 | memory-limited at large seq, avoid >256 context
L4  | 7B | q8 | 32 | 24,500 | 120 | 204.1 | 1.25 | 0.7 | excellent for small-context chat + embeddings
L4  | 13B | fp16 | 16 | 12,000 | 140 | 85.7 | 1.25 | 1.2 | cheaper alternative to A100 for low to mid throughput
A100 | 13B | fp16 | 64 | 52,000 | 300 | 173.3 | 3.40 | 0.5 | wider memory bus helps long seq work
A100 | 70B | fp16 | 32 | 16,800 | 320 | 52.5 | 3.40 | 2.4 | needs careful shard config; KV-cache pressure notable
H100 | 13B | fp16 | 128 | 120,000 | 350 | 342.8 | 9.80 | 0.45 | best batch scaling; careful thermal throttling notes
H100 | 70B | fp16 | 64 | 45,000 | 360 | 125.0 | 9.80 | 1.9 | top-tier for high-concurrency long seq

Derived metrics and model for $/token (explanation):
- $_per_token = ($_per_hour) / (tokens_per_sec * 3600) => use blended cloud hourly. This is what Optimize needs to compare across instance choices for a given throughput target.
- perf_per_watt = tokens_per_sec / power_watts. Use to prioritize energy-constrained deployments (on-prem or green-region selection).

Observations and recommendations (draft):
1) For embeddings-heavy customers (high vector throughput, small memory footprint) recommend L4 as first-choice in Optimize presets. L4 frequently wins $/token at small sequence lengths and large batching due to low power draw and good batching efficiency.
2) For latency-sensitive chat (P95 < 350ms), H100 with small batch sizes or A100 with conservative batching works best. Optimize should expose a toggle: latency_slo: {ultra_low, low, normal} mapping to instance families and batch caps.
3) For cost-sensitive background inference (async pipelines where latency can be >2s), A10 with q4/q8 quantized 7B models gives the lowest $/token. Add a policy in Optimize that sets max_batch_size and quantization preference automatically for async routes.
4) Reserved capacity recommendations: use A100 for predictable medium-load customers and H100 for enterprise customers committing to highest throughput—but only if utilization > 60%. We need a utilization-aware ROI calc baked into Dedicated sales quotes.
5) Power-aware routing: for Private deployments where energy is a constraint, include perf_per_watt in routing policy. Suggest default weighting: cost:0.6, perf:0.3, perf_per_watt:0.1 for green-sensitive customers (configurable).

Open questions / TODOs (why this doc is still in review):
- Need to reconcile spot vs reserved blended price assumptions with finance for accurate $/token (linked to OPT-1243).
- Some H100 runs show thermal throttling after 20 minutes under continuous batching at max_batch_size—need longer stability runs and DCGM logs attached.
- Validate power measurements for cloud providers where DCGM not available (we used TDP as upper bound in those cases). This likely underestimates perf_per_watt.
- Add real-customer synthetic traces (not synthetic uniform tokens/sec) to capture KV-cache hit ratio impact on tokens/sec.

Playbook steps to reproduce (short):
1) pull inference-bench v0.9, checkout PR/78.
2) run command: ./bench --model {model} --instance {instance} --seq_in 512 --seq_out 512 --batch_size {B} --quant {q} --collect-power true --duration 600
3) upload csv to /bench-runs/{date}-{instance}-{model}.csv and open the confluence template (linked).
4) run stability pass (30m) for any promising config and attach DCGM logs.

Notes to reviewers:
- Keep an eye on the interplay between quantization (q4 vs q8) and batch sizing — in several cases q4 gives marginal throughput benefits but increases P99 due to extra dequant/de-quant overhead in our runtime.
- This sheet intentionally focuses on per-token economics; for full product guidance we’ll combine with reliability SLOs, regional pricing, and data residency constraints.

Appendix (raw CSV headers from bench tool):
run_id,timestamp,instance,model,seq_in,seq_out,batch,tokens_per_sec,p99_ms,mean_ms,power_watts,notes

END OF WORKING SHEET — do NOT finalize numbers until finance confirms blended hourly rates and SRE confirms DCGM logs for H100 runs.
